section: Trends and regional pattern of poverty in India; poverty in Andhra Pradesh
subsections: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU

accepted.s: According to the Tendulkar poverty ratio for 2011-12, which State recorded the highest incidence of poverty among the following?
accepted.x: Chhattisgarh recorded the highest Tendulkar poverty ratio in 2011-12 at 39.93%.
accepted.tq: Use the exact percentage to distinguish the highest State from other high-poverty States.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State had the lowest Tendulkar poverty ratio in 2011-12?
accepted.x: Goa had the lowest Tendulkar poverty ratio in 2011-12, at 5.09%.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between low-poverty States using the stated ranking.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s: With reference to poverty in 2011-12, which one of the following States had the largest number of poor persons?
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh had the largest number of poor persons in 2011-12, estimated at about 5.98 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate the absolute number of poor persons from the poverty ratio.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups correctly represents the BIMARU and eastern belt States identified as having concentrated poverty?
o: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh
Goa, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat and Maharashtra
Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, Goa, Tamil Nadu and Odisha
Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Goa, Kerala, Sikkim and Gujarat
accepted.x: The high-poverty belt comprises Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
accepted.tq: Match the complete regional grouping rather than selecting a few familiar States.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Multidimensional Poverty Index for 2019-21:
1. Bihar had the highest MPI value among the States, at 0.16.
2. Kerala had the lowest MPI value, at 0.002.
3. Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand had MPI values of 0.103 and 0.131 respectively.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Bihar had an MPI of 0.16, Kerala 0.002, Uttar Pradesh 0.103 and Jharkhand 0.131.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement independently before choosing the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In the Rangarajan poverty line estimates updated by the RBI for 2022-23, which State had the highest rural poverty ratio?
accepted.x: Chhattisgarh recorded the highest rural poverty ratio at 25.1% under the 2022-23 Rangarajan-line estimates.
accepted.tq: Distinguish rural and urban values while identifying the highest State.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State recorded the largest number of persons exiting multidimensional poverty during 2013-14 to 2022-23?
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh recorded the largest number of exits, at about 5.94 crore, followed by Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Use the absolute number of exits rather than the State’s poverty ratio.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of the number of persons who exited multidimensional poverty during 2013-14 to 2022-23:
A. Rajasthan
B. Uttar Pradesh
C. Bihar
D. Madhya Pradesh
accepted.x: The correct order is Uttar Pradesh (5.94 crore), Bihar (3.77 crore), Madhya Pradesh (2.30 crore) and Rajasthan (1.87 crore).
accepted.tq: Rank the items by the numerical magnitude given for each State.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the changes in poverty recorded between 2011-12 and 2022-23?
o: Rural Odisha fell from 47.8% to 8.6%, while urban Bihar fell from 50.8% to 9.1%.
Rural Bihar fell from 47.8% to 8.6%, while urban Odisha fell from 50.8% to 9.1%.
Urban Odisha fell from 47.8% to 8.6%, while rural Bihar fell from 50.8% to 9.1%.
Rural Odisha fell from 50.8% to 9.1%, while urban Bihar fell from 47.8% to 8.6%.
accepted.x: Rural Odisha declined from 47.8% to 8.6%, and urban Bihar declined from 50.8% to 9.1%.
accepted.tq: Match each State with the correct rural or urban category and both endpoint values.
accepted.sec: Regional pattern - highest/lowest States, largest number of poor, BIMARU  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What was the all-India headcount poverty ratio in 1973-74 according to the Lakdawala basis?
accepted.x: The all-India poverty ratio in 1973-74 was 54.88% under the Lakdawala basis.
accepted.tq: Identify the year-basis combination before selecting the percentage.
accepted.sec: Poverty trends - all-India headcount by round, rural vs urban, recent estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the rural and urban poverty ratios in 1993-94?
accepted.x: In 1993-94, the rural poverty ratio was 50.1% and the urban ratio was 31.8%.
accepted.tq: Read the rural and urban columns together instead of using the all-India figure.
accepted.sec: Poverty trends - all-India headcount by round, rural vs urban, recent estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about India’s Tendulkar-based poverty ratios:
1. The all-India ratio declined from 37.2% in 2004-05 to 29.8% in 2009-10.
2. The rural ratio declined from 41.8% in 2004-05 to 33.8% in 2009-10.
3. The urban ratio declined from 25.7% in 2004-05 to 20.9% in 2009-10.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the decline in all-India, rural and urban poverty between 2004-05 and 2009-10.
accepted.tq: Verify the trend separately for the aggregate, rural and urban series.
accepted.sec: Poverty trends - all-India headcount by round, rural vs urban, recent estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Millennium Development Goal relating to poverty envisaged reducing the poverty ratio to which level by 2015, from 47.8% in 1990?
accepted.x: The MDG target was to halve poverty to 23.9% by 2015 from the 1990 level of 47.8%.
accepted.tq: Use the stated target rather than the later observed poverty estimates.
accepted.sec: Poverty trends - all-India headcount by round, rural vs urban, recent estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the recent poverty estimates based on the Tendulkar line?
accepted.x: The Economic Survey 2025-26 reports 4.7% for 2022-23 and 2.3% for 2023-24 under the Tendulkar line.
accepted.tq: Match the estimates to the correct years and poverty-line methodology.
accepted.sec: Poverty trends - all-India headcount by round, rural vs urban, recent estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the World Bank estimates of poverty between 2011-12 and 2022-23:
1. Rural poverty declined from 18.4% to 2.8%.
2. Urban poverty declined from 10.7% to 1.1%.
3. The urban decline was smaller than the rural decline in percentage points.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Rural poverty fell by 15.6 percentage points, while urban poverty fell by 9.6 percentage points, so statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Calculate the changes in both categories instead of relying on the final percentages alone.
accepted.sec: Poverty trends - all-India headcount by round, rural vs urban, recent estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the NITI Multidimensional Poverty Index estimates, India’s poverty headcount declined from 55.3% in 2005-06 to which percentage in 2022-23?
accepted.x: The NITI MPI headcount declined from 55.3% in 2005-06 to 11.28% in 2022-23, with an intermediate value of 14.96% in 2019-21.
accepted.tq: Track the endpoint year carefully in a three-period numerical series.
accepted.sec: Poverty trends - all-India headcount by round, rural vs urban, recent estimates  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: IKP — Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas
Velugu — District Poverty Initiatives Project, World Bank aided, run by SERP
MEPMA — Rural women’s SHGs established in 2000
SERP — Urban SHGs in municipal areas established in 2007
accepted.x: Velugu was the World Bank-aided District Poverty Initiatives Project implemented through SERP. MEPMA concerns urban SHGs, SERP rural mobilisation, and IKP was the renamed Velugu programme.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly matched institution by separating rural, urban and renamed programmes.
accepted.sec: AP poverty-reduction institutions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Velugu was renamed as Indira Kranthi Patham (IKP) in:
accepted.x: The Velugu programme was renamed Indira Kranthi Patham in 2004-05.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the launch year of the original programme from the year of renaming.
accepted.sec: AP poverty-reduction institutions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: MEPMA, established in 2007, primarily deals with:
o: Urban self-help groups in municipal areas
accepted.x: MEPMA, or Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas, works mainly through urban self-help groups.
accepted.tq: Ask which institution would handle poverty reduction in municipal rather than rural areas.
accepted.sec: AP poverty-reduction institutions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh poverty-reduction institutions is correct?
1. SERP focuses on social mobilisation of the rural poor into women’s SHGs and livelihoods.
2. MEPMA focuses on urban SHGs.
3. IKP was the renamed form of Velugu.
4. APMSS addresses poverty alleviation among rural and urban poor households.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe the roles or relationships of SERP, MEPMA, IKP and APMSS.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional division of rural, urban and combined responsibilities to test all statements.
accepted.sec: AP poverty-reduction institutions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In March 2026, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister handed over SHG loans amounting to:
accepted.x: In March 2026, ₹10,100 crore in SHG loans was handed over under SERP, MEPMA, Stree Nidhi, PMEGP and other schemes.
accepted.tq: Use the exact current-affairs figure and distinguish it from nearby rounded amounts.
accepted.sec: AP poverty-reduction institutions  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
SERP and MEPMA signed Memoranda of Understanding with which of the following institutions in March 2026?
1. Indian School of Business
2. XLRI
3. IIM-Visakhapatnam
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The MoUs were signed with the Indian School of Business, XLRI, IIM-Visakhapatnam and other institutions.
accepted.tq: Check whether each named partner belongs to the stated collaboration group.
accepted.sec: AP poverty-reduction institutions  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the Tendulkar estimates for 2011-12, Andhra Pradesh had a total poverty ratio of:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh had a total Tendulkar poverty ratio of 9.20% in 2011-12; its rural and urban ratios were 10.96% and 5.81%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the total ratio from the rural and urban components.
accepted.sec: AP poverty ratio vs all-India - Tendulkar 2011-12 and MPI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly compares Andhra Pradesh and India under the Tendulkar method for 2011-12?
o: AP rural 5.81%, urban 10.96%, total 9.20%; India rural 13.70%, urban 25.70%, total 21.92%
AP rural 25.70%, urban 13.70%, total 21.92%; India rural 10.96%, urban 5.81%, total 9.20%
AP rural 10.96%, urban 5.81%, total 9.20%; India rural 25.70%, urban 13.70%, total 21.92%
AP rural 9.20%, urban 10.96%, total 5.81%; India rural 21.92%, urban 25.70%, total 13.70%
accepted.x: The correct comparison is AP: 10.96% rural, 5.81% urban and 9.20% total; India: 25.70%, 13.70% and 21.92% respectively.
accepted.tq: Keep the order rural–urban–total unchanged while comparing the two jurisdictions.
accepted.sec: AP poverty ratio vs all-India - Tendulkar 2011-12 and MPI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the MPI for 2019-21, the multidimensional poverty headcount ratio of Andhra Pradesh was:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh had an MPI headcount ratio of 6.06% in 2019-21 and ranked ninth; India’s ratio was 14.96%.
accepted.tq: Separate the State’s total headcount from its rural, urban and national figures.
accepted.sec: AP poverty ratio vs all-India - Tendulkar 2011-12 and MPI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the trend in Andhra Pradesh’s Tendulkar poverty ratio?
accepted.x: AP’s poverty ratio declined successively from 44.6% to 29.9%, 21.1% and finally 9.20% across the stated years.
accepted.tq: Preserve the chronological order while tracking a declining numerical series.
accepted.sec: AP poverty ratio vs all-India - Tendulkar 2011-12 and MPI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The multidimensional poverty ratio in Andhra Pradesh declined from 41.6% in 2005-06 to approximately what level according to the cited 2023 estimate?
accepted.x: The cited APPSC-GS 2023 figure records a decline in AP’s multidimensional poverty from 41.6% to 21%.
accepted.tq: Distinguish this estimate from the later 2019-21 MPI figure of 6.06%.
accepted.sec: AP poverty ratio vs all-India - Tendulkar 2011-12 and MPI  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which social group has the highest poverty ratio in India according to the Tendulkar estimates for 2011-12?
accepted.x: Scheduled Tribes had the highest poverty ratio among social groups; rural ST poverty was about 45%, followed by Scheduled Castes.
accepted.tq: Use the social-group ranking rather than the overall rural or urban ranking.
accepted.sec: Social group poverty  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following statements is correct regarding social-group and educational disparities in poverty?
1. Scheduled Tribes have a higher poverty ratio than Scheduled Castes.
2. In Andhra Pradesh, districts with large tribal populations tend to have higher poverty.
3. Poverty among persons with no formal education was 35.1%, compared with 14.9% among those with post-secondary education.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Tribal concentration and lower educational attainment are associated with higher poverty in the stated estimates.
accepted.tq: Combine social-group, regional and education-based dimensions without confusing correlation categories.
accepted.sec: Social group poverty  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which district had the highest MPI poverty headcount ratio among the districts listed for Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Kurnool had the highest listed MPI poverty headcount ratio at 12.84%, with an MPI of 0.054.
accepted.tq: Identify the maximum value while separating it from other high-poverty districts.
accepted.sec: District-level poverty in AP - backward districts, ITDA, regions

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the MPI poverty headcount ratio in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Vizianagaram’s MPI poverty headcount ratio was 8.66%. The figure 6.13% belongs to East Godavari, while Prakasam recorded 6.28%.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped numerical value by checking each district against the table.
accepted.sec: District-level poverty in AP - backward districts, ITDA, regions

accepted.s: Which of the following districts were identified as belonging to the higher-poverty group in addition to the principal high-poverty districts?
accepted.x: Prakasam, with 6.28%, and East Godavari, with 6.13%, were also included in the higher-poverty group.
accepted.tq: Distinguish supplementary high-poverty districts from the lowest-poverty group.
accepted.sec: District-level poverty in AP - backward districts, ITDA, regions

accepted.s: Which regional pattern of poverty is correctly associated with Andhra Pradesh?
o: Rayalaseema and North Coastal Andhra are poorer, while delta districts are generally least poor.
Delta districts and Coastal Andhra are poorer, while Rayalaseema is least poor.
Only urban districts of Rayalaseema show higher poverty.
All districts of Coastal Andhra have uniformly high poverty, irrespective of geography.
accepted.x: Poverty is higher in Rayalaseema districts such as Kurnool and Anantapur and in North Coastal Andhra, while delta districts are generally least poor.
accepted.tq: Use the regional contrast rather than judging districts by coastal or inland labels alone.
accepted.sec: District-level poverty in AP - backward districts, ITDA, regions

accepted.s: The poorer areas of North Coastal Andhra are particularly associated with:
o: Deltaic irrigation and intensive paddy cultivation
accepted.x: The higher-poverty pattern in North Coastal Andhra is associated with tribal and ITDA agency tracts, including areas around Vizianagaram and Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Apply the regional pattern to identify the geographical setting linked with poverty.
accepted.sec: District-level poverty in AP - backward districts, ITDA, regions

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as an area requiring attention for poverty reduction in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Expansion of luxury housing in metropolitan areas
accepted.x: The identified areas include schooling, drinking water, sanitation, bank accounts, child-adolescent mortality and nutrition; luxury housing is not included.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated multidimensional poverty concerns.
accepted.sec: District-level poverty in AP - backward districts, ITDA, regions
